transaction_findings.finding: Validity checks backup address and string name. Low-level create omits URL and permits explicit upsert; Logic normal path allocates. Registry enforces nonempty bounded ASCII name, persists URL, typed IDs, actor and activation height checks. Declared corrected behavior, not literal parity.

Actual ClearList.getList reads attestations; ordinary Type7-created whitelist fails lookup. Native create fields admin/backup also differ from validator expected adminAddress/backupAddress. Runtime Registry intentionally repairs lifecycle. Source evaluator preserves dependency name/field behavior, but backend mocks do not prove real storage integration.

Nonzero list requires primary admin only. List0 permits self-cert and protocol-admin BANLIST command. Revoke validation tests active direct membership; repeat issue has no duplicate check and overwrites address-keyed row. Registry intentionally rejects list0, rejects active duplicates, scopes rows by (list,address), omits revoke reason and has no root payload.

These validators call ClearList dependencies; 4/19/20 can request derived membership. Source evaluator depends on supplied backend observations. There is no demonstrated wiring from exact JS storage/full BIP32 into accepted Rust economic transactions. Send recipient lookup and banlist fallback quirks are source-preserved boundaries.

runtime_registry: Declared intent/corrected behavior retained; no runtime parity claim
